title: Hypotheses of the products
doc: Lists the ions that the chemistry says could be there, each with the source that proposed it: the parent times the photocatalytic rules (one or two steps), the offline suspect index, the expected members of the families already found, and lists the user typed or imported. One pass, fixed order, byte-identical on every run. A hypothesis is a place to look and what the search finds is graded afterwards.

references.note: transformation products generated from a parent and screened as suspects in a non-target workflow

parent.title: Parent compound (formula, or SMILES for the rules with groups)

hypotheses.title: Hypotheses: formula, m/z, adduct, source and weakest prediction level

max_steps.title: Chained reactions
max_steps.description: Most reactions chained from the parent; one hypothesis per net change of formula, the fewest steps first

max_suspects.title: Most suspects
max_suspects.description: Hypotheses taken from the suspect index, the best supported first; the number left out is written in the registry

other_polarity.title: Other polarity too
other_polarity.description: Expected members of a family in the other polarity too ([M-H]- of a positive base and the reverse)

nominal.title: Unit resolution
nominal.description: Two formulas of the same nominal m/z and adduct are one hypothesis, the others its alternatives

algorithms.title: Rules, suspects, families and lists
algorithms.doc: Parent times the rules of TP_Mine/data/regole_tp.json (profile of the campaign), merged with the other sources by net formula change; ids follow the order of m/z (crates/mzlab-feat/src/hypo/sources.rs). Prediction level 2 literature, 3 class, 4 generic.

applicability.note: Rules with groups need the structure of the parent; without it the fallback rules are used

title: Filters of the products
doc: Hides a row for the first filter it fails: F1 peak quality, F2 isotopologue of another row, F3 as strong in the controls as in the treated samples, F4 constant ratio to the parent (in-source fragment or adduct), F5 formula error beyond the tolerance of the file. Rows are marked, not deleted. The decoys (rule deltas shifted by a mass defect) say how many matches are by chance.

references.note: decoys give the number of matches by chance

table.title: Feature table of the treated samples and the controls
Rows that pass F1-F5, with the filter that hid the others

tol_min.title: Lowest formula tolerance
tol_min.description: Floor of the tolerance of a formula; the tolerance of a file is its measured error, kept between the two

decoy_ppm.title: Decoy tolerance
decoy_ppm.description: A decoy lies beyond this many ppm of every true delta, and a row matches a decoy within it

algorithms.title: Five stages in a fixed order
algorithms.doc: The first filter that hides the row wins (first_hidden in crates/mzlab-feat/src/interp/filtri.rs); the registry filtri/1 holds the text and the counts of each stage.

title: Link the MS2 of the products
doc: Gives each row that passes the filters the modification it carries (formula change from the parent and isotope check of the MS1 at the apex), every DDA MS2 of its series with the purity of the isolation, and the comparison of the fragments with the MS2 and the MSn tree of the parent. Evidence for the chemist: it never names the product.

references.note: components linking a parent and its products by MS2 similarity

tp.title: Rows with their modification, linked MS2 and comparison with the parent

select_ppm.title: Isolation centre
select_ppm.description: An MS2 scan belongs to a row when its isolation centre is within this many ppm of the m/z of the row

purity_min.title: Lowest purity
purity_min.description: A scan below this purity is chimeric and does not vote

match_ppm.title: Formula tolerance
match_ppm.description: Tolerance of the modification (neutral formula change) and of the comparison of the fragments with the parent

algorithms.title: Pooled MS2 of the series
algorithms.doc: Pools the clean scans whose isolation centre lies on the row into one consensus spectrum (select and consensus in crates/mzlab-feat/src/interp/ms2link.rs, as mzFinder pools the MS2).

algorithms.title: Isomers from the fragment traces
algorithms.doc: Compares the traces of the strongest fragments across the scans of one row and says when two groups of fragments rise and fall apart, so two isomers co-elute under one row.

applicability.note: A row with fewer clean scans than the minimum is not split

iso_corr.title: Fragment correlation
iso_corr.description: Correlation between the traces of two fragments below which they belong to different isomers

title: Position of the modification
doc: Says which classes of sites of the parent the MS2 of a product is compatible with, never which site it is: classes are excluded, supported or undistinguished, the sublevel is 3a only when at least one class is excluded and at most three remain, and the rest is 3b. The reactivity of the parent is shown beside as a prior and does not decide.

references.note: an MS3 fragment that carries the modification separates positional isomers

tp.title: Product row with its consensus MS2

sites.title: Classes of sites with their support and the declared confidence

match_ppm.title: Fragment tolerance
match_ppm.description: Matching of the fragments with the cleavages of the parent (HR spectra)

min_rel.title: Informative fragment
min_rel.description: A fragment is informative from this share of the base peak, if its formula is within 5 ppm

min_informative.title: Fewest informative fragments
min_informative.description: Fewer informative fragments cannot tell one class from the others

margin.title: Margin of the lead
margin.description: Log-likelihood units a class must lead the second by to be called alone: two fragments' worth of evidence

algorithms.title: Votes of the MSn tree
algorithms.doc: The likelihood of each class is read from the fragments of the MSn tree that carry the modification (votes_of in crates/mzlab-feat/src/interp/sito.rs).

applicability.note: Votes from the MSn tree of the product when it was recorded (source tree)

algorithms.title: Likelihood from the cleavages
algorithms.doc: Without the tree, the likelihood of a class is built from the cleavages of the parent that explain the peaks of the MS2 (match_spectrum in crates/mzlab-feat/src/chem/posizioni.rs).

references.note: aliphatic OH loses water more than phenol; N-oxides give [M+H-O]+: observed losses are evidence shown, not a filter

ll_support.title: Supported fragment
ll_support.description: Log-likelihood a fragment that a cleavage explains adds to a class

ll_against.title: Unexplained peak
ll_against.description: Cost of a peak a class cannot explain, twice the support: a wrong site is worse than an undecided one

title: Draw the modification
doc: Chooses the simplest form that tells the truth about a product: the structure itself only when the position is a site, a multicenter bond when every candidate lies in one aromatic ring, otherwise a bracket around a zone or the whole parent. Never one structure per site. The page draws it over the coordinates of the parent that Ketcher gives; without them the structure becomes a bracket.

sites.title: Classes of sites with their support and the declared confidence

drawing.title: Drawn form: mode, atoms, bracket or ring, faint atoms, highlighted zone

algorithms.title: Structure, multicenter or bracket
algorithms.doc: The mode follows the position report: structure for a site, multicenter for candidates in one ring, bracket otherwise; atoms a loss removes are drawn faint and dashed (drawing in crates/mzlab-feat/src/interp/disegno.rs).

title: Draw a structure
doc: Opens the structure editor (Ketcher, in a sandboxed frame inside the page) so the student draws the parent or a product. A partial structure carries a Δ in a bracket or an attachment on any atom of a ring, which makes it a level 3 candidate and never an identification.

structure.title: SMILES, with the Δ or the multicenter attachment of a partial structure (parz/1) when one is drawn

algorithms.title: Ketcher editor
algorithms.doc: Interactive: the output is the drawing at the moment the step is read (TPDraw.smiles and TPDraw.partial in mzlab/web/draw.js). No engine runs and no .wasm is loaded.

title: Reactivity of the parent
doc: Computes where the parent is most reactive toward an electrophilic radical (condensed Fukui function f(-) per atom and per class of C-H sites). The result is a prior shown beside the sites of tp.position and never decides one: the experiment does.

reactivity.title: Fukui functions per atom and C-H sites with their rank

conformers.title: Conformers
conformers.description: ETKDG conformers of the parent, lowest energy first; f(-) is also computed on the lowest ones to give its spread

protomer.title: Form of the parent
protomer.description: none: the SMILES as written; ph7: the most probable charge form at pH 7 from a table of typical pKa

algorithms.title: GFN2-xTB with Fukui functions
algorithms.doc: ETKDG geometry, GFN2-xTB of the neutral molecule, the cation and the anion at the same geometry; f(+), f(-), f(0) and the dual from the Mulliken charges, f(-) also on the lowest conformers for its spread; C-H sites by symmetry class (reactivity_json in crates/mzlab-chem/src/reatt.rs).

references.note: the semiempirical method of the neutral molecule, the cation and the anion
condensed Fukui functions from the charges of N-1, N and N+1 electrons

algorithms.title: Extended Hückel fallback
algorithms.doc: One diagonalisation, no SCC and no ions; used by the engine only when an SCC of GFN2-xTB does not converge, and the result says so in its method (eht.rs).

applicability.note: Fallback: the engine picks it, the user does not
